description: Knowledge base for suggesting and matching study groups based on student profiles

primary_factors.description: Same department students share course material and understanding
Students at similar academic levels face similar challenges
Shared enrolled courses create natural study partnerships
Compatible learning styles improve group dynamics

secondary_factors.description: Similar study commitment levels reduce friction
Mixed performance can enable peer teaching
Overlapping free time is essential for group meetings

group_types.purpose: Focus on a specific course, share notes, solve problems together
group_types.best_for: Students taking the same course who want to improve understanding
group_types.structure: Weekly meetings, rotating topic leaders, shared note documents

group_types.best_for: Students with exams in the same course within 2 weeks
group_types.structure: Daily or every-other-day sessions, practice questions, mock exams

group_types.purpose: Collaborate on course projects or assignments
group_types.best_for: Students with complementary skills working on group projects
group_types.structure: Regular check-ins, clear task division, shared workspace

group_types.purpose: Hold each other accountable for study goals and habits
group_types.best_for: Students who struggle with consistency and motivation
group_types.structure: Daily check-ins, shared goal tracking, mutual encouragement

group_types.purpose: Diverse perspectives from different departments for broader learning
group_types.best_for: Students interested in interdisciplinary projects or research
group_types.structure: Bi-weekly meetings, knowledge sharing sessions, collaborative projects

high_compatibility: Same department + same level + shared courses
Similar learning styles + similar study hours
Complementary strengths (one strong in theory, another in practice)
moderate_compatibility: Same department but different levels (mentoring opportunity)
Different learning styles but same courses (diverse perspectives)
Similar performance levels with different schedules
low_compatibility: No shared courses or academic interests

group_success_tips: Set clear expectations and ground rules from the start
Assign a rotating group leader for each session
Create a shared document or chat group for communication
Each member should prepare before group sessions
Start and end sessions on time — respect everyone's schedule
Balance teaching and learning — everyone contributes
